messages.author: a9e2e9ac319971b0
messages.subject: sampling function with kronecker matrix
parts:
Hi, I am new to Stan, and I am trying to write a hierarchical bayesian model in Stan. 
For my model, I would like to do a multivariate normal sampling with kronecker matrix, I saw some discussion about the kronecker matrix but I don't know whether it is feasible in Stan now? 
For example, can we call a function such as below ?
y ~ multi_normal(vector mu, kronecker_matrix)
where
kronecker_matrix = matrix A (x) matrix B

If not, what would be a good way to write this function in Stan? 
Thanks in advance for your help!

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: sampling function with kronecker matrix
parts:
On Sunday, April 3, 2016 at 4:46:32 PM UTC-4, Haoyan Sun wrote:
Hi, I am new to Stan, and I am trying to write a hierarchical bayesian model in Stan. 
For my model, I would like to do a multivariate normal sampling with kronecker matrix, I saw some discussion about the kronecker matrix but I don't know whether it is feasible in Stan now? 
For example, can we call a function such as below ?
y ~ multi_normal(vector mu, kronecker_matrix)
where
kronecker_matrix = matrix A (x) matrix B
If not, what would be a good way to write this function in Stan?

There is this R code that you could adapt to Stan code in the case where the Kronecker product is part of a quadratic form, as in the case of a multivariate normal

K <- 25L
D <- diag(1 + runif(K))
a <- runif(1)
W <- round(matrix(runif(K^2), K, K))
W[upper.tri(W, TRUE)] <- 0
W <- W + t(W)
Lambda <- Harman23.cor$cov[1:4,1:4]
y <- rnorm(K * ncol(Lambda))
mult <-
  function(D, a, W, Lambda, y) {
    temp <- Lambda %*% matrix(y, nrow = ncol(Lambda))
    # optimize this particularly if D - a * W is sparse!!!
    scalar <- t(y) %*% c(apply(D - a * W, 1, "%*%", t(temp)))
    return(scalar[1])
  }

all.equal(c( t(y) %*% kronecker(D - a * W, Lambda) %*% y ), 
          mult(D, a, W, Lambda, y))
Ben

messages.author: a9e2e9ac319971b0
messages.subject: Re: sampling function with kronecker matrix
parts:
Thanks Ben and Seth! 
I still don't quite understand how to incorporate Ben's code into my stan code.

Basically what I am doing is to model random coefficient beta_i with individual predictors. Say beta_i is i*3 matrix, Z_i is individual predictors data, an i*4 matrix

beta_i ~ multi_normal(Z_i*delta, Vbeta)

So I need to give priors for delta and Vbeta. Vbeta is a 3*3 matrix that could be an inverse-whishart distribution similar to covariance matrix formation. However it's difficult for me to write the prior for delta.

Say prior for delta conditioning on vbeta follows:
vec(delta) ~ multi_normal(vec(deltabar), Vbeta(x)Adelta)

where deltabar is 4*3 zero matrix, Adelta is a 4*4 precision matrix. but how can I express "Vbeta(x)Adelta" in stan? 

Thanks!!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] sampling function with kronecker matrix
parts:
> On Apr 4, 2016, at 3:10 PM, Haoyan Sun <haoy...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Thanks Ben and Seth!
> I still don't quite understand how to incorporate Ben's code into my stan code.
>
> Basically what I am doing is to model random coefficient beta_i with individual predictors, say beta_i is i*3 matrix, Z_i is individual predictors data, a i*4 matrix

>
> beta_i ~ multi_normal(Z_i*delta, Vbeta)
>
> So I need to give priors for delta and Vbeta. Vbeta is a 3*3 matrix that could be an inverse-whishart distribution similar to covariance matrix formation. However it's difficult for me to write the prior for delta.
>
> Say prior for delta conditioning on vbeta follows:

>
> where deltabar is 4*3 zero matrix, Adelta is a 4*4 precision matrix. but how can I express "Vbeta(x)Adelta" in stan?

You just want to break that Kronecker product down
and save the repeated parts as a temporary variable. I don't
know the details, but that's how it has to work out. You
do not want to just build an enormous covariance matrix, because
then we have to solve it, but won't know the structure at the point
it needs to be solved.

We prefer scaled LKJ to inverse Wishart.

- Bob
